E1.evidence: The issue documents an intermittent CI test failure with its log: "Here's an example error we see on the CI from time-to-time:" followed by the log lines "Expected: is approximately 508.18968922836888 (absolute error <= 9.9999999999999995e-07)" and "Actual: 508.19 (of type double), which is -1.0207e-06 from 508.19" (https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/issues/1235).

units_identified: transmission_interface gtest executables (same package's own tests)
E2.evidence: The failure is a floating-point comparison tolerance inside transmission_interface's own unit tests; the issue asks to "Improve the robustness of transmission tests by making sure all floating-point value comparisons are using an approximate equality check" and notes "The `EPS` value used for these tests could perhaps be relaxed slightly too" (https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/issues/1235). The fix touches only files under transmission_interface/test/, e.g. "-const double EPS = 1e-6;" / "+const double EPS = 1e-5;" and "-  EXPECT_EQ(50.0, actuator_reduction[0]);" / "+  EXPECT_THAT(50.0, DoubleNear(actuator_reduction[0], EPS));" (https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/pull/1238/files). No value crosses a boundary between two separately deployable units; the test and the code under test ship in one package, and the defect is the test's own tolerance.

notes: Exit step: E2 step 2 (internal): test-only tolerance change in ros2_control's transmission_interface tests. PR #1238 merged 2023-12-20 into master, merge commit e92b6c2c84946c8dab44146a5b4a666390543d61; the issue was closed by christophfroehlich: "I think this was solved by #1238?".
